name: West Malagasy Sakalava
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Dahl, Otto Chr. 1951. Malgache et Maanjan: une comparaison linguistique. Oslo: Egede-Instituttet (Glottolog Glottolog's most extensive description sketch for Sakalava). Peace Corps 1996 manual reached: scanned, no stress statement.

sources.citation: Ferrand, Gabriel. 1909. Essai de phonétique comparée du malais et des dialectes malgaches. Paris: Geuthner.
sources.note: Chap. VI 'L'accent tonique' (pp. 236-245) states general Malagasy rules: radical stems are generally paroxytone (disyllables) or proparoxytone (trisyllables), rarely oxytone; monosyllables accented; suffixation shifts the accent one vowel to the right; reduplications/compounds keep accent only on the last element. The chapter names no Sakalava variety; it is a Merina-based general statement, not a description of skg.

sources.citation: Jully, Antony. 1901. Manuel des dialectes malgaches (hova, betsileo, tankarana, betsimisaraka, taimorona, tanosy, sakalava (mahafaly), soahely). Paris: J. André.
sources.note: scanned text has no occurrence of 'accent'. Its 'sakalava' is the Mahafaly variety (Glottolog codes it to Mahafaly, not skg).
